parts.text:
```yaml
- id: DR-01
  requirement: >
    The service must not manage its own user accounts or passwords and must
    instead authenticate staff using accounts issued outside the service by the
    platform company.
- id: DR-02
  requirement: >
    The service must isolate each drone operating company's data so that its
    fleet, jobs, sites, flights, and operational problems are visible only to
    that company's staff and cannot be viewed by other operating companies or
    by the platform's airspace desk.
- id: DR-03
  requirement: >
    The service must protect the personal data of staff in accordance with the
    GDPR, including minimizing exposure of personal identifiers across roles
    and tenants and supporting required data protection controls.
- id: DR-04
  requirement: >
    The service must allow a fleet technician to add new drones to their
    operating company's fleet and to retire existing drones so that retired
    drones can no longer be used for flights.
- id: DR-05
  requirement: >
    The service must allow a fleet technician to take a drone out of service
    for repairs and return it to service when repairs are complete, preventing
    drones that are out of service from being assigned to or signed off for a
    flight.
- id: DR-06
  requirement: >
    The service must allow a fleet technician to set up charging pads at their
    company's sites, maintain the working status of charging equipment, and
    send a drone to charge at an available charging pad.
- id: DR-07
  requirement: >
    The service must represent sites with their concurrent takeoff and landing
    capacity and must enforce that the number of drones taking off or landing at
    a site at the same time does not exceed that site's available places.
- id: DR-08
  requirement: >
    The service must allow the platform's airspace desk to maintain a shared
    airspace picture accessible to all operating companies, consisting of the
    network of flight corridors between sites and the zones that group those
    corridors.
- id: DR-09
  requirement: >
    The service must allow the platform's airspace desk to enter airspace
    closures announced by the authorities for prohibited zones, supporting both
    planned closures with a specified start and end time and sudden closures
    that take effect immediately.
- id: DR-10
  requirement: >
    The service must allow the platform's airspace desk to amend an existing
    airspace closure during the day, including widening the affected zones or
    changing the closure's end time, and immediately update the shared airspace
    picture.
- id: DR-11
  requirement: >
    When an airspace closure is entered or amended, the service must report to
    the airspace desk the aggregate disruption caused across customer companies
    without exposing any single operating company's fleet, jobs, sites, or
    specific operational problems.
- id: DR-12
  requirement: >
    The service must assist a dispatcher in identifying which of their
    company's available drones can reach the starting site of a job, taking
    into account drone availability, battery charge, and reachable flight
    corridors.
- id: DR-13
  requirement: >
    The service must never automatically select or assign a drone or a flight
    route for a job; a licensed dispatcher must explicitly choose both the
    drone and the flight corridor route for every flight.
- id: DR-14
  requirement: >
    The service must require a licensed dispatcher to explicitly sign off on a
    flight after choosing its drone and route before the flight is permitted to
    depart, and must record the dispatcher's sign-off for compliance with EU
    drone operation and EU U-space rules.
- id: DR-15
  requirement: >
    The service must prevent a flight from being signed off or departing if its
    chosen route passes through a zone with an active closure or a planned
    closure that overlaps the flight's window.
- id: DR-16
  requirement: >
    The service must allow a dispatcher to call off a flight of their operating
    company either before departure or while the flight is in progress.
- id: DR-17
  requirement: >
    When a sudden, planned, or amended airspace closure comes into force while
    drones from one or more operating companies are already in the air, the
    service must immediately identify all affected in-flight and scheduled
    drones and alert each affected operating company's dispatcher.
- id: DR-18
  requirement: >
    The service must ingest drone telemetry reports received through relay
    stations in a way that tolerates patchy radio coverage by deduplicating
    repeated reports, ordering out-of-order reports by event timestamp rather
    than arrival time, handling late reports without corrupting current drone
    state, and detecting missing reports when communication drops out.
- id: DR-19
  requirement: >
    The service must preserve the active flight state of a drone that restarts
    in flight after an onboard software fault and continues flying, associating
    subsequent telemetry reports with the ongoing flight rather than treating
    the restart as a new or terminated flight.
- id: DR-20
  requirement: >
    The service must monitor actual in-flight battery drain against remaining
    flight requirements—accounting for faster battery depletion in cold or
    windy conditions—and alert the responsible dispatcher when a drone's battery
    depletes faster than planned.
- id: DR-21
  requirement: >
    Because a single dispatcher may be responsible for hundreds of drones at
    once, the service must proactively surface exceptions and alerts—such as
    airspace closures affecting active flights, faster-than-planned battery
    drain, in-flight restarts, or lost radio contact—so the dispatcher does not
    have to manually watch every drone continuously.
```
